subject: Immediate runtime patch activation request — brief customer impact
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Ruiz <daniel.ruiz@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 May 2028 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Immediate runtime patch activation request — brief customer impact

Daniel — quick note from ops: we observed a sudden increase in tail-latency on the inference fleet serving your us-west clusters (correlated with a memory-fragmentation pattern in the runtime allocator). The on-call team verified degraded 99.9th percentile latency affecting a small subset of GC pods.

We recommend applying a short emergency hotfix to the runtime that addresses the allocator fragmentation and prevents multi-second tail spikes. The patch is tiny (runtime allocator tweak + KV cache guard) and the canary plan is 1% traffic for five minutes, then ramp to 10% and full rollout if green. Expected customer-facing impact: a handful of 1–3 second reconnects during canary activation (clients will transparently reconnect). Overall SLOs should be preserved except for brief spikes during the very short canary steps.

Proposed maintenance window: immediate / rolling, starting now — total expected disruption per pod ~30–90 seconds during the canary step. If you need us to hold, we can schedule within the next 30 minutes, but we recommend rolling now to avoid further tail events.

Attachments: hotfix_release_notes_v1.2.pdf (notes + canary checklist), rollback_playbook.md (rollback steps).

Action requested: please reply YES to authorize immediate rolling canary on your us-west clusters, or reply with preferred delay window. If you have strict network/whitelist constraints, let us know now.

Thanks — Ava
Ava Chen
Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference

On Fri, 4 May 2028 at 14:07, Daniel Ruiz <daniel.ruiz@acme-corp.com> wrote:
> Ava — thanks for the heads up. We will authorize the canary now. Two quick asks before you proceed...

Short answers:
- No token loss / inference-state loss expected. The patch modifies allocator behavior and inserts a KV-cache-safe fence. In-flight requests will either complete or be retried by the client; we are not dropping responses mid-stream. We tested with synthetic long-before-commit streams and confirmed graceful reconnects.
- Billing / SLA: a standard brief interruption during a canary does not automatically trigger credits. If we see a sustained SLO breach (>5m sustained 99.9 violation) we'll follow the SLA process; that's unlikely given the plan, but we'll monitor and keep you informed.

Canary plan (high level):
1) Push hotfix image to canary nodes (1% traffic) — healthchecks and p95/p99 monitored.
2) If healthy after 5 minutes, 10% ramp for 10 minutes.
3) Full rollout if green.
4) Automatic rollback to last image on any >3 error-rate spike or >200ms tail-latency regression.

Mitigations we have in place: circuit-breaker fallback to smaller model instance for affected calls, prefix-cache pinned to avoid cold-kv reads, and immediate alerting to both our infra on-call and Acme's SaaSOps.

I'll start the canary now unless Ava asks us to pause. Running the first step will take ~2 minutes to shift traffic and confirm health.

— Dev
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime Team | Redwood Inference

Thanks Daniel — we are proceeding with the rolling canary now. Current status:
- 14:16 PT: hotfix image pushed to canary nodes (1% traffic). No errors observed.
- 14:21 PT: p95/p99 trending back to normal for affected slots.
- 14:26 PT: ramped to 10% traffic for second step. No user-facing exceptions reported yet.

Next steps: hold at 10% for 10 minutes, then full rollout if metrics remain green. We will post an all-clear and a short postmortem note within 24 hours summarizing root cause, what changed, and follow-up mitigations (longer-term allocator fix schedule).

If you see any issues on your side (timeouts, auth errors, or dropped connections), please reply immediately and we will roll back the canary. Thanks for the quick approval and for looping SaaSOps.

Best — Ava
